body.statement: Relative to \(\mathcal D_\rho\), \(\beta\) is identified at every \(\theta\in\mathcal B\) and, for every \(k\) with \(Q_Ac_k\ne0\), equals \(\langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle/\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2\).  At every \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\), \(\theta\) and \(S\theta\) induce the same collection \(\{P_e:e\in\mathcal E\}\), both belong to \(\mathcal D_\rho\), and have distinct effects \(\beta\) and \(\beta+\gamma/\alpha\).  Hence \(\beta\) is identified in \(\mathcal D_\rho\) if and only if \(r^\star<\infty\).  The finite-breakout clause answers the multi-environment case isolated after Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6: every pairwise two-environment analysis may retain the source ambiguity while the joint law of \(E\ge d+2\) environments identifies \(\beta\) under the stated profile restriction.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: the first environmental cumulant flag exactly separates the identified and source-label-ambiguous regions.
body.gap: Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, prove two-environment nonidentification under simultaneous source shifts and leave joint multi-environment rescue open; no published result supplies this iff projected-plane frontier.
body.consumer: For a selected edge in the Sachs perturbation panel, the theorem either returns a direct-effect functional under the maintained profile restriction or records an exact structural ambiguity rather than a spurious estimate.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\theta\in\mathcal B\).  By definition, \(r^\star\leq R_{\max}<\infty\), so at least one \(k\) has \(Q_Ac_k\neq0\).  The cumulant-cancellation lemma gives \(Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k\), and taking the Euclidean inner product with \(Q_Ac_k\) yields
\[
 \beta=\frac{\langle Q_Ac_k,Q_Am_k\rangle}
 {\lVert Q_Ac_k\rVert_2^2}.                          \tag{9}
\]
Every quantity on the right of (9) is a functional of the observed laws: cumulants give \(c_k,m_k\), the first \(d\) treatment contrasts give \(C\), and the calibration-rank assumption gives \(Q_A\).

To prove identification rather than merely derive a moment equation, let \(\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal D_\rho\) induce the same collection of observed laws.  Then it has the same \(c_k,m_k,C,A,Q_A\), and \(r^\star\).  In particular its breakout is finite, so the disjoint definition of the two branches places \(\widetilde\theta\) in \(\mathcal B\).  Applying (9) to \(\widetilde\theta\) gives \(\widetilde\beta=\beta\).  Thus \(\beta\) is identified relative to the full domain at every point of \(\mathcal B\).

Now let \(\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\), and set
\[
 V_e=\alpha\epsilon_{u,e},\qquad W_e=\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad q=\gamma/\alpha.
\]
The treatment-loading lower bound permits the division by \(\alpha\).  The observed variables can be written
\[
 T_e=V_e+W_e,
 \qquad
 Y_e=(\beta+q)V_e+\beta W_e+\epsilon_y.              \tag{10}
\]
Under \(S\theta\), the latent and treatment sources are \(W_e\) and \(V_e\), while the coefficients are \(1,\beta+q,-q\).  Hence
\[
 T'_e=W_e+V_e,\qquad
 Y'_e=(\beta+q)(W_e+V_e)-qW_e+\epsilon_y
      =(\beta+q)V_e+\beta W_e+\epsilon_y.            \tag{11}
\]
Equations (10)--(11) prove equality of the complete observed laws, not only equality of their moments.  The definition of \(\mathcal N_\rho\) already supplies \(S\theta\in\Theta_\rho^\circ\) and \(r^\star(S\theta)=\infty\).  For completeness, it also implies that \(S\theta\) itself belongs to \(\mathcal N_\rho\).  Indeed,
\[
 S^2\theta=(1,\beta,\gamma/\alpha,
             \{\alpha\epsilon_{u,e},\epsilon_{t,e}\}_{e\in\mathcal E},
             \epsilon_y).                            \tag{12}
\]
The loading value one is legal because it is the loading of \(S\theta\); the effect and confounding bounds in (12) are inherited from \(\theta\); and the two source families in (12) are exactly the two source families of \(S\theta\) in the opposite order, so their centeredness, independence, entire moment generating functions, and moment bounds are inherited.  Its latent contrasts are \(\alpha^k u_k\in A\), and its observed laws, calibration gap, and infinite breakout are unchanged by (10)--(11).  Thus \(S^2\theta\in\Theta_\rho^\circ\) with infinite breakout, proving \(S\theta\in\mathcal N_\rho\subset\mathcal D_\rho\).

Finally, the two effects differ by \(q=\gamma/\alpha\), whose magnitude is at least \(q_0>0\).  Therefore no observed-law functional can equal both, and \(\beta\) is not identified at any point of \(\mathcal N_\rho\).  Since \(\mathcal D_\rho=\mathcal B\cup\mathcal N_\rho\), the two arguments prove the claimed if-and-only-if frontier.  The final comparison in the statement adds no mathematical premise: the swap algebra is already explicit in (10)--(11), whereas (9) uses the joint environmental plane and a nonzero complementary direction, which requires the multi-environment geometry proved below.
